text:
maria: Heads up — canary rollout v2.14.0 showing a sustained token/sec drop starting at 11:12 UTC. 37% lower than baseline on p100 clusters. This started immediately after the merge of PR #3412 and the gated deploy at 11:05.

alex: I see it in traces too — long queueing at the continuous-batcher startup window. Warmup looks stuck for ~3–8s per worker.

ben: metric snapshot: `canaryA token/sec 840 -> 530`, `p50 latency +120ms`, `small-batch count up +18%`. Nothing else unusual in infra.

deploy-bot: Deploy v2.14.0 to canary started 11:05 UTC (PR #3412 merged by ken).

ken: FYI #3412 touched scheduler startup heuristics (prefetch thresholds) and the kernel-selection fallback path that runs during cold KV cache. Could be an interaction.

jitendra: quick grep of the worker logs shows a repeating pattern:

```
[11:12:34.123] continuous-batcher: entering startup_ramp (seq_len=16)
[11:12:34.127] kernel: selected fallback_path (packed_copy=false)
[11:12:34.129] kvcache: miss -> warming, stall token drain
[11:12:37.453] continuous-batcher: drain after warmup (3.324s)
```

alex: That 3s warmup per worker multiplies across the pool and correlates with token/sec drop. The kernel fallback path seems to force extra memcopy because it thinks quantized kernels aren't safe until KV entries present.

maria: Anyone seen this in CI perf? I thought we had a perf gate.

ben: CI perf did show a tiny regression in the scheduler microbench but it was under threshold so the merge passed. The post-merge end-to-end load test wasn't run for the exact config (startup-heavy workload).

ken: I can try a quick bisect locally between master~2 and HEAD to confirm PR blame. Can we get a minimal repro job that simulates many short-start sessions?

alex: I pushed a stress job to perf-runner: `startup-heavy-seq16-2000conns`. Link: https://perf.internal/runs/1590 (profiling artifacts uploaded).

sre-bot: Alert: canary token/sec drop > 25% for 5m — paging: eng-runtime on-call.

maria: Thanks. Ken, tag me when you have a bisect candidate. Alex — any flamegraphs?

alex: Uploaded flamegraph. Key hotspot: memcopy in kernel fallback and scheduler waiting on `kvcache.init()` on first request. The fallback path does a synchronous KV prefetch that blocks batch construction.

alex: snippet from flamegraph summary: `kernel::fallback_memcopy 42%`, `batcher::wait_on_kvcache 31%`, `scheduler::awake_rate_limiter 9%`.

ken: Ran quick bisect: commit range where perf drops lines up with a change that flips `scheduler.prefetch_mode` to `aggressive_on_start` (PR #3412). Reverting that flag locally stops the warmup stalls.

jitendra: So aggressive prefetch triggers kernel fallback that synchronously blocks until KV warms. Two things collide: prefetch tries to populate KV, kernel fallback doesn't like missing entries and does heavy memcopy, and batcher waits for KV warm signal. That explains the startup-ramp stall.

maria: Proposed mitigation: revert prefetch change in canary immediately and run a controlled canary rollback. Also open a follow-up to make kvcache.prefetch async and the kernel fallback non-blocking.

ken: I created a revert PR (PR #3418-revert). Can we hold the rollout until revert lands?

deploy-bot: Rollout hold requested by @maria on canary v2.14.0 — pausing automated promotion.

ben: Quick patch idea: change scheduler startup loop to allow `batcher.drain()` after X ms rather than waiting on kvcache warmup. Temporary guard reduces stall from 3s to ~200ms in my local run.

alex: Can we run that as a hotfix on canary to measure impact while the revert goes through? If hotfix helps, we can promote then merge a proper fix.

maria: Yes run hotfix as canary-only. ken / ben coordinate and post results. Also add a perf gate test for startup-heavy workload so this doesn't slip again.

ken: Hotfix deployed to canary at 11:48 UTC: changed startup drain timeout to 200ms. Early stats: token/sec recovered to 790 (vs 530), p50 latency back to +30ms. Still slightly off baseline but much better.

jitendra: Filed follow-ups: "async-kvcache-prefetch" and "kernel-fallback-nonblocking". Assigning to runtime team for priority.

maria: Good. I'll merge the revert once CI completes and keep rollout paused until verified. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: Revert PR #3418 submitted; CI started.

alex: NOTE for postmortem — add a startup-heavy perf test, and instrument kernel fallback path with a warmup sampling metric so we can detect blocking memcopies.

maria: Will write a short postmortem draft after root cause confirmed. For now, canary hold + hotfix + revert in flight.

ben: Leaving logs and perf artifacts in the thread: https://internal.artifacts/run/1590 and flamegraph link above.

maria: closing loop — once revert CI passes we'll coordinate a controlled re-rollout with gating on the new startup perf test.

ken: thumbs. Thanks all.
